author: agent
objective: Among residents of the 96 mainland French departments, what was the adjusted association between department-level long-term mean PM2.5 (1999–2016) and cumulative in-hospital COVID-19 death counts/rates on 1 May 2020?

scientific_invariants.research_question: Among residents of the 96 mainland French departments, what was the adjusted association between department-level long-term mean PM2.5 (1999–2016) and cumulative in-hospital COVID-19 death counts/rates on 1 May 2020?
scientific_invariants.target_outcome_and_population: Cumulative in-hospital COVID-19 deaths through 2020-05-01 among residents of 96 mainland French departments; count model with department population offset.
scientific_invariants.principal_contrast: Rate ratio per 1 µg/m³ increase in department-level long-term mean PM2.5
principal_variants: Adjusted continuous-PM2.5 negative-binomial model at 1 May 2020 with population offset
Article-reported adjusted PM2.5-quartile model (Q2/Q3/Q4 vs Q1) at 1 May 2020
prohibited_evidence: Prior reanalysis code, source manifests, or results

article_evidence.finding: Methods report 96 mainland departments, 1999–2016 GOME/NASA SEDAC 1-km PM2.5 aggregated by department, cumulative hospital COVID deaths, and fully adjusted negative-binomial models.
Supplementary material is retained for inspection of article-linked tabular supporting information; any PM2.5 fields will be excluded from fitted data.

article_evidence_map.model: article.txt Statistical analysis and Table 3: PM2.5 and temperature together; beds, medical density, age 60+, male share, unemployment, poverty, urban population, density and diabetes.
